## Design

### 2026-10-10 – Week 1 – Designing My First Custom PCB

**8h**

Week 1 – Designing My First Custom PCB
During this session, I worked on designing and finishing my first custom PCB in KiCad. I started by building the schematic and connecting all of the components, including the XIAO ESP32-C3, DHT11 sensor, OLED display, buttons, resistor, and the connector for the MPU6050.
After finishing the schematic, I assigned the correct footprints to each component and transferred everything into the PCB Editor. One of the most challenging parts was arranging the components and routing all of the connections without creating conflicts. I had to move several components and redo some traces multiple times until everything could be connected correctly.
I also wanted the PCB to feel like my own project instead of simply copying the example from the guide. I created a custom spaceship-shaped board outline inspired by the LUNARIS-01, a spaceship from another project I am working on. I also added LUNARIS-01 text and custom space-themed silkscreen artwork with a planet and rings.
After routing the board, I ran KiCad's Design Rules Checker. The board showed 0 unconnected items. The remaining two courtyard errors came from the imported display footprint and are the same errors shown as acceptable in the Starbie guide. I also checked that adding the custom silkscreen artwork did not introduce any new errors.
This session taught me a lot about how a schematic becomes a physical PCB, how footprints and routing work, and how PCB layout sometimes requires reorganizing components instead of trying to force traces through a bad layout. It was challenging, especially since this was my first time doing this, but by the end of the session I had a routed and customized PCB that I was happy with.
